subject: Dedicated capacity planning: model memory mapping and precision tradeoffs
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@aperturetx.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aperturetx.com
Date: 2028-10-01T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — model footprints + quant tradeoffs

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough today. We're excited about moving forward with a reserved pool for our primary inference workload (clinical summarization + search). Before we commit, procurement needs the following from Redwood:

- Per-model memory footprint estimates at our target context lengths (8k, 32k) including KV cache overhead.
- Two precision scenarios: fp16 baseline and int8 post-quantization (expected accuracy drift tolerance ~1-2% for our LLM ops).
- Concurrency assumptions to map to a reserved GPU count for 99th percentile latency < 250ms for generate requests (we expect 12 concurrent sustained workers).
- A suggested canary plan and minimum commit for pilot (6 weeks).

Attached is our short requirements doc and a sample request pattern. Can you send a compact mapping (per-model bytes + recommended reserved GPU count per scenario) and a short note on operational implications?

Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-03T11:14:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: per-model memory mapping (8k vs 32k) + quant assumptions

Team — initial draft attached as CSV and summarized below. Numbers assume baseline model profiles similar to 70B decoder-only architectures with typical KV encoding overhead. Latency SLOs are not baked into these bytes; they are pure GPU memory working set estimates.

Summary table (high level):
- Model A (70B, opt encoder-decoder style):
  - 8k context, fp16: model weights + optimizer states (host) — 60 GB; KV cache per active session ~ 2.4 GB; working set per concurrent request ~ 15 GB (shared weights on device, per-session KV pinned).
  - 32k context, fp16: KV cache per session ~ 9.6 GB; working set per concurrent request ~ 22 GB.
  - int8 quantized (post-quant): weight footprint reduces ~2.5x on-device; KV cache compression depends on approach — we assume ~1.9x savings for a standard KV quant scheme (so 8k KV ~1.26 GB, 32k KV ~5.05 GB).

- Model B (13B high-throughput assistant):
  - 8k fp16: model + weights on device ~12 GB; KV per session ~0.45 GB; working set ~3.5 GB.
  - 32k fp16: KV per session ~1.8 GB; working set ~6 GB.
  - int8: model weights ~4.8 GB on-device; KV compression ~1.8x.

Assumptions and notes:
- We assume shared model weight resident per GPU, so per-GPU headroom = max(concurrent session KV sum assigned to that GPU) + safety margin (recommended 25%).
- For your expected 12 sustained concurrent workers, distribution/packing strategy matters: pinning fewer larger sessions to each GPU vs many small sessions changes tail latency.
- Quantization reduces model weight memory most; KV caching gains are smaller but meaningful at 32k. For models that are KV-intensive (long-document summarization), int8 can cut reserved GPU counts by ~20-35% depending on packing.

I've attached kv_memory_model_map.csv with per-model rows and a per-GPU suggested packing for 1,3,6,12 concurrent workers. Please review and I'll refine if you want iso-latency targets included.

Marissa
Staff Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv_memory_model_map.csv (CSV, 14 KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved pool sizing + pricing implications (pilot vs annual)

Putting operational guidance on top of Marissa's numbers:

Operational recommendation:
- Pilot (6 weeks): reserve 6x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs with the following packing: 2 GPUs for Model A (32k, fp16 baseline, canary load), 2 GPUs for Model B mixed traffic, 2 GPUs as headroom/failover + canary. This maps to ~40% of the expected sustained commit and keeps tail latency buffer.
- 12-month commit: for steady-state at your 12 concurrent workers and using int8 quant for Model A, we estimate 9 reserved GPUs. If you keep fp16 at 32k, estimate 12-13 GPUs.

Pricing impact (high level):
- Pilot: pro-rated monthly for 6 GPUs at standard reserved pilot rate — see attached workbook for month-by-month cost.
- Commit: 12-month pricing shows ~18% discount vs monthly, 24-month ~28%. We can carve a custom SLA and a usage offset for your canary if you want to accelerate procurement.

Risk notes:
- Accuracy regression: int8 quant introduces ~1-2% expected delta; recommend a small eval set in production and an automatic rollback policy.
- KV cache fragmentation: long-tail sessions may cause higher VRAM fragmentation — recommend periodic defragmentation and KV eviction policies in the runtime.

Attaching reserved_capacity_pricing.xlsx and I'll upload a short canary runbook.

Priyom
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reserved_capacity_pricing.xlsx (XLSX, 36 KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, procurement@aperturetx.com
Date: 2028-10-05T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — recommended pilot and next steps

Alex — consolidated recommendation below and a proposed next step timeline.

What we recommend for Aperture pilot:
- Pilot pool: 6x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs for 6 weeks. Allocation: 2 GPUs (Model A canary, fp16, 32k), 2 GPUs (Model B mixed), 2 GPUs (headroom & failover).
- Quant path: start with fp16 in pilot; enable int8 quant in week 3 on a canary subset (10% traffic) once your eval set passes the quality gates. If quant passes, we convert the steady-state plan to the int8 column (saves ~20-30% reserved GPUs).
- Operational runbook: small canary steps, auto-rollback on eval metric drift >1.5%, KV eviction TTLs set to 30 min for interactive users. Runbook link: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/canary-aperture
- Deliverables from us: finalized per-model packing CSV, pricing workbook, and a short pilot SLA addendum for procurement.

Next steps (timeline):
1) Procurement signs pilot SOW (target Oct 9) — Sean will send SOW draft.
2) Redwood provides pilot pool and kickoff runbook (Oct 11).
3) Canary testing (Oct 12–Oct 25), with int8 trial starting Oct 16 if canary passes early checks.

I've attached the pilot SOW draft and the three files Marissa/Priyom produced; procurement: please confirm legal/PO path and whether you need an explicit data residency or KMS note for the pilot.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to go through the spreadsheet numbers.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
